intermediate_exposition_in_order: On admitted reduced parts 0<x≤1, write I(x)=x, S(x)=x², K(x)=1 and F(x)=cast(2x). Finite word evaluation satisfies E([],x)=x and E(f::w,x)=E(w,f(x)); induction gives E(u++v,x)=E(v,E(u,x)). The identities I(x)=I(y)⇒x=y and K(x)=K(y)=1 identify the identity and constant behaviors. If S(x)=S(y), positive cross-values have equal squares. If either cross-value were strictly smaller, monotonicity of positive multiplication would make its square strictly smaller too. Both strict alternatives are impossible, so the cross-values agree and reduced-ratio identity forces x=y. For 0<x<1, multiplication by positive x preserves x<1, giving x²<x. Repeated application yields S^n(x)<x for every positive n, excluding a return; x=1 is fixed. Finally F(1/2)=F(1)=1 with 1/2≠1, while F(1/3)=2/3 and F(2/3)=1/3. Fold is therefore noninjective and has a nonstatic recurrent pair.
